Someone by the fire nods at the counter. "We pool food here. Keep what you need for the road — the rest feeds everyone, once it's food."

Daniyar spends the afternoon with the small tree with mitten-shaped leaves (three shapes), spicy root smell — look, smell, the smallest taste, then waiting. By evening daniyar is thoroughly, educationally sick. "NOT food," they announce to the fire, pale. "My body told me so." The lesson is learned
The Journal notes it: Sassafras — NOT food. (Daniyar tested it.)

Dragonfly the size of a hawk. Gamey. The wings are like cellophane. It's dead. The carcass is there on the ground — search the body if you want the meat. But you don't know this flesh. Clean it, test it cautiously, or ask someone who knows. And don't leave it long: meat rots where it lies.
Taken: Gland sac x1, Gland sac x1, Glasswing Darter (carcass) x1.
Nothing edible. (Glasswing Darter (carcass) — not food yet: A carcass. Clean it with a knife — quickly. Spoils fast..)

Daniyar sets aside time with the Glasswing Darter flesh. Look, smell, touch — then the smallest taste, and wait. An hour passes. Calm stomach. Another hour. Nothing. "It's food," Daniyar tells the fire. "You know it in your gut. Literally." The Codex notes it.
